list.name: node
list.label: Node suffix
list.description: The suffix that -statshostname appends to every node-emitted metric key, including the leading dot (e.g. ".mynode"). Leave empty for a node started without -statshostname, which is how statoshi.info runs.

panels.description: Total, inbound and outbound connection counts. The address-family and node-type splits are broken out on the connection-composition panels below, so plotting all eight overlapping slices here just made the totals hard to read.
panels.title: Peers

panels.description: Size of the address manager's peer database. Split out because it is roughly 600x the connection count, so on a shared axis it hid every connection series.
panels.title: Known Addresses

panels.description: Round-trip ping latency to peers at the lower bound, median and upper bound, in microseconds. The series come from ping_us, so they are microseconds; the previous nanosecond unit made every reading a thousand times too large.
panels.title: Peer Pings

panels.description: Reject messages sent, stacked by reason. The per-reason series are mutually exclusive and sum to the 'all rejects' series, so a stack shows both the total rejection rate and its composition. As nineteen unstacked bars this was unreadable.
panels.title: Reject Messages Sent

panels.description: Outbound connects and disconnects per second. Inbound accepted is also plotted but that counter is not in the current build; the two outbound series carry the churn signal.
panels.title: Connection Churn

panels.description: Closes split by connection type. Listed explicitly because a wildcard would also match each type's .lifetimeSeconds sibling.
panels.title: Connections Closed by Type

panels.description: Average lifetime at close, per type. A flood of one-second block-relay closes looks nothing like normal churn, and neither was visible before.
panels.title: Connection Lifetime at Close

panels.description: Inbound evictions per second on the left axis, with the age of the evicted connection on the right. The age is in seconds and is one to two orders of magnitude larger than the eviction rate.
panels.title: Inbound Evictions

panels.description: Inbound slot usage against the configured maximum, with total connections for context. The slot gauges are not in the current build, so only total connections plots today.
panels.title: Inbound Capacity

panels.description: Current peer count split by connection type. A donut reads the composition at a glance; the timeseries below still shows how it changed over time.
panels.title: Peers by Connection Type (current)

panels.description: Peer transport protocol mix over time, stacked to show the whole. BIP324 (v2) adoption is easier to read as a filled share than as three overlapping lines.
panels.title: Peers by Transport Protocol (stacked share)

panels.description: Connections by type as a stacked area. The types are mutually exclusive and sum to the connection total, so the stack height is the peer count.
panels.title: Peers by Connection Type

panels.description: Connections by transport protocol as a stacked area: cleartext v1, BIP324 v2 and peers still being probed. The band height is the connection total.
panels.title: Peers by Transport Protocol

panels.description: Age of the oldest and newest connection. A newest age stuck near zero means constant churn; oldest age tracks how long the longest-lived peer has been with us.
panels.title: Connection Age

panels.description: Inbound connections by network, stacked. The networks are mutually exclusive, so the stack shows both the inbound total and its composition.
panels.title: Inbound Connections by Network

panels.description: Outbound connections by type and network, stacked. Each combination occupies its own part of the outbound total.
panels.title: Outbound Connections by Type and Network

panels.description: Entries in the new and tried address tables.
panels.title: Address Manager Size

panels.description: Addresses entering the manager, and why the rest were rejected.
panels.title: Address Manager Ingest

panels.description: Failed attempts to pick an address to connect to. Non-zero means the node is running out of usable peers.
panels.title: Address Selection Misses

panels.description: Bootstrap health. A silent DNS seed regression was previously undetectable.
panels.title: DNS Seed Results

panels.description: Bans actually applied by banman, and addresses discouraged from being served.
panels.title: Bans & Discouragement

panels.description: Peer misbehaviour, stacked by reason. The reasons are mutually exclusive and the stack height is the total misbehaviour rate.
panels.title: Misbehavior by Reason
